reading.body:
This 25,600-square-foot facility in Bridgewater holds 2.3 MW of installed power with 20 MW more available on site, totaling 22.3 MW of announced capacity. At an assumed 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 22.3 MW of IT load would support roughly 560 racks of accelerator infrastructure. The campus ranks fifth among the five data centers in New Jersey with published power figures, accounting for approximately 20 percent of the state's total announced capacity of 111.3 MW.

The facility certifies to PCI DSS, HIPAA, SOC 1, SOC 2, SSAE 18, and ISAE 3402 standards, qualifying it for regulated workloads in financial services and healthcare. No Tier classification is published. The operator does not publish whether the site has dedicated power infrastructure, whether it connects to the grid or on-site generation, or what constraints exist on reaching the stated 20 MW expansion figure.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities overall, but only five publish power capacity, making this site one of very few with transparent specifications in the state. Whether 22.3 MW of announced capacity in a northeastern market is material to AI scaling depends on whether that power is actually available and whether the operator intends to serve GPU-intensive workloads, neither of which is stated in the published record.
